correctness.rationale: Define a closed nonempty word by a proper nonempty border with exactly two occurrences, allowing overlaps, and singleton as closed. For a binary de Bruijn circular word B of order h, any closed factor with border length >=h would repeat an h-factor at two distinct cyclic starts, impossible for factor length <=N=2^h; thus b<h. For each starting position and b<h, at most one complete first return exists, yielding upper bound 2+(h-1)N distinct circular closed factors. Linear closed-factor lower bound N holds for any cut of length N; linear factors embed among circular ones. For h=5, exhaustive directed de Bruijn graph local switches (2^16 pairings) and independent edge-simple Euler tours both give the 2048 rotation classes; independent direct border and first-return counts agree: 93:360,94:888,95:600,96:200, mean 1509/16, variance 195/256. An independent local 2048-cycle re-enumeration reproduced that histogram. The computer proof is exhaustive only at h=5; universal bound uses the injection.

value.rationale: Closed factors encode complete first returns; de Bruijn universal cycles are a natural extremal family. The all-order O(N log N) upper bound separates their return complexity from quadratic unrestricted closed-rich words. The complete h=5 census is a natural finite classification (all 2048 distinct cycles, four consecutive attainable counts), furnishing exact invariant distribution, moments and benchmarks, not arbitrary slices.

limitations: Count excludes empty word and lengths>N.
All-order bound may not be sharp; h=5 numerical distribution does not extrapolate.
Rotation classes counted once using unique 00000 edge.
